newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's Pannon GSM to issue HUF 24 bln bond.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's Pannon GSM to issue HUF 24 bln bond.

text.p: Hungarian mobile telephone company Pannon GSM will issue inflation-indexed bonds totalling 24 billion forints ($138 million) nominal value on the Hungarian market, company and bank officials said on Thursday.
"This is the biggest corporate bond issue in modern Hungary," said Farbod Lotfi, Director of the issue manager ING Barings Rt.
Pannon will auction three-year (series A), four-year (series B) and five-year (series C) bonds of eight billion forints nominal value for each series on February 20, he said.
"Hungarian institutional investors are our main target," Lotfi added.

The bonds bear an interest rate of year-on-year CPI plus three percent, to be adjusted semi-annually, with interest added to the capital annually and the interest and capital to be paid on the day of maturity.
Series A bonds mature on February 25, 2000, series B on February 26, 2001 and series C on February 26, 2002.
Capital and interest repayment is guaranteed by ING Bank NV, and the maximum permitted oversubscription is nine billion forints.
Pannon GSM bonds are expected to be listed on the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) on March 5 or 6, pending BSE council approval, Lotfi said.

Pannon, which forecasts its number of subscribers to reach 308,000 by the end of 1997 from 170,000 at the end of 1996, plans to spend most of the money raised on infrastructure development, the company said.
"We plan to use 80 percent of the amount raised towards network expansion," said Gussi Emri, Pannon GSM General Director.
-- Denes Albert, Budapest newsroom +36 1 327 4040 ($ = 173.8 Hungarian Forints)
